summary: The enterprise AI model API landscape in 2026 is dominated by the three hyperscalers—AWS Bedrock, Azure OpenAI (now within Microsoft Foundry), and Google Vertex AI—each offering managed access to multiple foundation models within the customer's existing cloud security perimeter. There is no single winner; the best fit depends on existing cloud footprint, required model breadth, and governance needs. Data-platform-native options (Snowflake Cortex, Databricks) and governance-focused platforms (IBM watsonx) are gaining traction, while edge-focused providers like Cloudflare Workers AI and Oracle Cloud AI round out the field.
why_enterprises_use_aggregators: Data residency and security: inference runs inside the company's own cloud VPC/perimeter so sensitive data never leaves their controlled environment or gets used to train third-party models.
Compliance and governance: aggregators provide SOC 2, HIPAA, ISO, FedRAMP and audit-logging controls out of the box, satisfying regulated-industry requirements that raw vendor APIs often cannot.
Single billing and consolidated contracts: model usage rolls into existing cloud spend commitments (EDPs, MACC), simplifying procurement and leveraging negotiated discounts.
Model choice behind one API: a single integration gives access to many providers (Claude, Llama, Mistral, Gemini, GPT, etc.), reducing vendor lock-in and easing model swapping.
Leveraging existing cloud investments: identity (IAM/Entra), networking, monitoring, and security tooling already in place extend seamlessly to AI workloads without new vendor onboarding.

platforms.name: Azure OpenAI Service / Microsoft Foundry
available_models: select open models via Foundry Model Catalog
platforms.pricing: Pay-as-you-go per 1K/1M tokens plus Provisioned Throughput Units (PTUs) for reserved capacity; bills against Azure commitment.
platforms.best_for: Microsoft-first shops wanting first-party access to OpenAI models within existing Azure governance and identity.

platforms.name: AWS Bedrock
platforms.pricing: On-demand per-token pricing plus Provisioned Throughput for reserved capacity; integrated into AWS billing.
platforms.best_for: AWS-centric enterprises wanting the widest multi-provider model choice behind a single API.

platforms.name: Google Vertex AI Model Garden
platforms.pricing: Pay-per-token on-demand plus Generative AI Scale Units (GSUs) for reserved throughput (e.g., 25 GSUs of Gemini 2.5 Flash ≈ 67,250 tokens/sec sustained).
platforms.best_for: Google Cloud shops and teams wanting Gemini plus the broadest Model Garden selection and strong data/ML tooling.

platforms.name: Snowflake Cortex AI
platforms.pricing: Consumption-based, billed in Snowflake credits per token/compute; rolls into Snowflake platform spend.
platforms.best_for: Enterprises with governed data in Snowflake wanting LLM access to their data without it leaving the warehouse (5,200+ weekly active accounts in FY2026).

platforms.name: Databricks Mosaic AI
platforms.pricing: Consumption-based on Databricks compute/DBUs; model serving and foundation model APIs billed per usage.
platforms.best_for: Data engineering and ML teams wanting to build, fine-tune, and serve custom models on their lakehouse data.

platforms.name: IBM watsonx
platforms.pricing: Capacity/token-based pricing plus enterprise licensing; flexible on-prem, hybrid, and cloud deployment.
platforms.best_for: Regulated enterprises with existing IBM relationships prioritizing governance, explainability, and long-term platform flexibility.

platforms.name: Oracle Cloud Infrastructure (OCI) Generative AI
platforms.pricing: Per-character/per-token on-demand plus dedicated AI cluster hosting for reserved capacity.
key_features: integration with Oracle DB and Fusion apps
platforms.best_for: Oracle database and ERP/Fusion customers wanting GenAI close to their Oracle data estate with dedicated capacity.

platforms.name: Cloudflare Workers AI
platforms.pricing: Pay-per-use based on neurons/inference units; low-cost serverless pricing with generous free tier.
platforms.best_for: Developers and enterprises needing low-latency edge inference and a lightweight gateway to proxy and govern multiple model providers.
